mainTopic: Blood and stains layered on a garment (כיבוס and חציצה), then the new פרק's משנה on which כהנים receive a share of the קדשים and hides.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ruling: חטאת blood soaked in underneath, with עולה blood on top, still requires כיבוס. רבא asks about the reverse order and decides that no laundering is needed, because what counts is the garment absorbing the חטאת blood. רבא then teaches that a stain on a garment is a חציצה during טבילה, unless the owner's work makes that stain normal for him, like a טבח with blood or a מוכר רבב with fat. He asks about a garment with both blood and fat. The גמרא shows the question is only real for someone who does both jobs, and it ends in תיקו. With that, פרק דם חטאת ends. A new משנה begins about which כהנים get a share of the קדשים. A טבול יום, a מחוסר כפורים and an אונן get no share, while בעלי מומין do get a share and eat but may not offer. The משנה's general rule is that a כהן unfit for עבודה gets no meat and no hides, even if he was טמא only at the sprinkling of the blood. Its source is the פסוק that gives the portion to 'the one who offers the blood.'

steps.title: Sin-offering blood below and burnt-offering blood above
steps.stepSummary: The ruling ends: when חטאת blood is underneath and עולה blood is on top, the garment needs כיבוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the blood of a חטאת is on the bottom and the blood of an עולה is on top, the garment must be laundered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ruling that began before this section. The case is a garment that already soaked up חטאת blood and then got עולה blood on top of it. Laundering is required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only חטאת blood creates a duty of כיבוס. Here the חטאת blood was already soaked into the garment before the עולה blood landed on top. Covering it with other blood does not cancel the duty. This sets up רבא's question about the reverse order.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin offering; its blood on a garment requires laundering
Burnt offering; its blood does not require laundering
Laundering the garment
Below / above, meaning which layer of blood is on the bottom and which is on top

phrases.english: The blood of a sin offering is below
and the blood of a burnt offering is above,
it requires laundering.

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּם חַטָּאת לְמַטָּה וְדַם עוֹלָה לְמַעְלָה, טָעוּן כִּיבּוּס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ruling from before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חטאת blood absorbed underneath, with עולה blood on top, still requires כיבוס.

steps.title: רבא asks about the reverse order
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks about עולה blood underneath and חטאת blood on top: is the reason for כיבוס touching or absorption?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asks: if the עולה blood is on the bottom and the חטאת blood is on top, what is the law? Is laundering required because the blood touches the garment, and here it does touch? Or is it required because the garment absorbs the blood, and here the garment did not absorb it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא flips the order of the previous case and asks whether the garment needs laundering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer depends on what triggers כיבוס. If simply touching is enough, the חטאת blood on top touches the garment. If the garment must actually soak it up, the garment is already full of עולה blood, so the חטאת blood was never really absorbed.

keyTerms.meaning: Asks (introduces an open question)
Touching
Absorbed
Or perhaps

phrases.english: Rava asks:
The blood of a burnt offering is below
and the blood of a sin offering is above, what is the law?
Is it because of touching?
And this blood does touch.
Or perhaps it is because of absorption?
And this garment did not absorb it.
phrases.notes: The garment was already soaked with the עולה blood. Some versions leave out the word in round brackets.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverses the order of the case in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether כיבוס is triggered by the blood touching the garment or by the garment absorbing it.

steps.title: רבא resolves: no laundering needed
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers his own question: such garments do not need כיבוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא later answered his own question: these garments do not need to be laundered.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers his own question: no laundering is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling implies that absorption is what matters. Since the garment was already full of עולה blood, the חטאת blood was not absorbed, so there is no duty of כיבוס.

keyTerms.meaning: He later resolved it himself
Require

steps.whatToRemember: חטאת blood underneath requires laundering. חטאת blood landing on top of absorbed עולה blood does not, because absorption is what counts.

phrases.english: He then resolved it,
that they do not require laundering.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No כיבוס is required; absorption is the deciding factor.

steps.title: Stains as a barrier during immersion
steps.stepSummary: רבא says it is obvious that blood or fat on a garment is a חציצה, unless the owner works with that substance.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is obvious to me that blood on someone's garment is a barrier. But if he is a butcher, it is not a barrier. Fat on his garment is a barrier. But if he sells fat, it is not a barrier.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא states two clear rules about immersing a garment. A stain blocks the water, unless the owner's job makes that stain normal for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something counts as a חציצה only if the person cares about it being there. A טבח does not mind blood, and a מוכר רבב does not mind fat. So for them, that kind of stain does not block the טבילה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious to me
Forms a barrier between the water and the garment during immersion
Butcher
Fat or grease stain
Fat seller

phrases.english: Rava said: It is obvious to me,
that blood on his garment interposes,
phrases.notes: This is about immersing a garment in a מקוה. A barrier makes the immersion not work.

phrases.english: but if he is a butcher, it does not interpose.
Fat on his garment interposes,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם מוֹכֵר רְבָב הוּא – אֵינוֹ חוֹצֵץ.
phrases.english: but if he is a fat seller, it does not interpose.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new, related topic: stains on garments during טבילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A stain is a חציצה unless the owner is used to that stain and does not mind it.

steps.title: רבא asks about blood and fat together
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks what the law is when the garment has both blood and fat on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asks: if there is blood and fat on his garment, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks a new question that builds on his two rules: what if both kinds of stain are on the garment?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each rule on its own was obvious. The question is whether having both stains together changes the result.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the law?

phrases.english: Rava asks:
Blood and fat on his garment, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רָבָא: דָּם וּרְבָב עַל בִּגְדּוֹ, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Combines the two cases from step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether blood and fat together on a garment count as a חציצה.

steps.title: The question seems pointless
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא's question: for a טבח the fat is clearly a barrier, and for a מוכר רבב the blood is clearly a barrier.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he is a butcher, the fat should already make it a barrier! And if he sells fat, the blood should already make it a barrier!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's question by arguing that the answer is already obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each person minds the stain that does not come from his own job. A טבח minds fat, and a מוכר רבב minds blood. Either way, one of the stains is a חציצה, so it seems there is nothing to ask.

keyTerms.meaning: Let me derive it from (another reason that already settles it)
And if

phrases.english: If he is a butcher,
let me derive it from the fat!
And if he is a fat seller,
let me derive it from the blood!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם טַבָּח הוּא, תִּיפּוֹק לִי מִשּׁוּם רְבָב
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's question about blood and fat together.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Whatever his job, one of the two stains is unfamiliar to him and so is clearly a חציצה.

steps.title: The case of someone with both jobs
steps.stepSummary: The question is about someone who is both a butcher and a fat seller. Does he mind having two stains together?
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the question is needed for someone who does both this job and that job. Is it that he does not mind one stain but does mind two? Or perhaps he does not mind even two?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא's question by giving a case where it really is in doubt: a person who works with both blood and fat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This person is used to each stain separately. The open issue is whether having both stains at once is enough to make him mind. If he minds, the stains are a חציצה; if he does not, they are not.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for (a specific case)
This and that, meaning both jobs
Minds, cares about it
About two

phrases.english: No, it is necessary
for one who does this and that.
phrases.notes: He works as both a butcher and a fat seller.

phrases.english: Is it that he does not mind one,
but does mind two?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִּלְמָא אַתַּרְתֵּי נָמֵי לָא קָפֵיד?
phrases.english: Or perhaps he does not mind two either?

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question seemed pointless, because one stain would always be unfamiliar to the person.
steps.terutzMaskana: The question is about someone who works with both, and asks whether two familiar stains together make him mind.

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The question about the man with both jobs is left open: תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand: the question is not resolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the discussion without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source settles whether two familiar stains together count as something the owner minds. So the law in this case stays in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question remains unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: A stain is a חציצה only if the owner minds it. Whether someone who works with both blood and fat minds having both on one garment is left unresolved.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question from step 7 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The case of blood and fat on the garment of someone who works with both remains in doubt.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק דם חטאת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא formally finishes the פרק called דם חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק דם חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: This line is not part of the argument. It marks the end of the פרק we just finished, which ended with the תיקו about the butcher who also sells fat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן formula is a traditional goodbye to a finished פרק, expressing the hope to come back and learn it again. The next line begins a brand-new topic with a new משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: "We will return to you". This is the formula said when finishing a פרק.
"The blood of a חטאת". These are the opening words and the name of the פרק that just ended.

phrases.english: We will return to you, "The blood of a sin offering"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק right after the תיקו in Step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: פרק דם חטאת is complete. A new פרק begins next.

steps.title: A טבול יום and a מחוסר כפורים get no share of the meat
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that a טבול יום and a מחוסר כפורים do not get a share of the קדשים, even to eat it that evening.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A טבול יום and a מחוסר כפורים do not get a share of the קדשים to eat in the evening.
steps.whatsHappening: The new פרק opens with a משנה about dividing sacrificial meat among the כהנים. Its first rule is that a טבול יום and a מחוסר כפורים do not get a portion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both of these כהנים are not yet fully pure. A טבול יום still has to wait for nightfall (הערב שמש). A מחוסר כפורים, such as a זב or מצורע, still has to bring his קרבן. The משנה says they get no share even though the טבול יום would be allowed to eat once night comes.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. It marks where the משנה text begins.
Someone who was טמא, immersed today, and must wait until nightfall to be fully טהור.
Someone who still has to bring a קרבן to finish becoming טהור, such as a זב or מצורע.
They take a share, meaning they receive a portion when the meat is divided.
In the evening, meaning after nightfall.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the טבול יום gets a share because he will be pure tonight. The משנה says clearly that he gets no share, even to eat later in the evening.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who immersed that day
and one lacking atonement
phrases.notes: He means someone who still has to bring his purification קרבן, like a זב or מצורע.

phrases.english: do not receive a share of the sacrificial meat
to eat it in the evening.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק and a new topic after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A טבול יום and a מחוסר כפורים receive no portion of the קדשים, even for eating that night.

steps.title: The אונן may touch the meat but may not offer or take a share
steps.stepSummary: An אונן may touch קדשים, but he may not offer קרבנות and gets no share to eat in the evening.
steps.simpleTranslation: An אונן may touch, but he may not offer, and he does not get a share to eat in the evening.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves on to a second type of כהן, the אונן, a mourner on the day a close relative died. It gives three rules for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אונן is not טמא, so touching the meat is allowed. Still, he may not do the עבודה, and like the טבול יום he gets no portion to eat that evening.

keyTerms.meaning: A mourner on the day his close relative died, before the burial.
Touches. He is allowed to handle the sacrificial meat.
Offers a קרבן, meaning he does the עבודה.

phrases.english: An acute mourner may touch
phrases.notes: The corrected wording leaves out the round-bracket word אינו, so read it as "he may touch." An אונן is not טמא.

phrases.english: but he may not sacrifice offerings,
and he does not receive a share to eat in the evening.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second type of כהן to the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אונן may touch קדשים but may not offer them and receives no portion for the evening.

steps.title: Blemished כהנים get a share and eat but do not offer
steps.stepSummary: בעלי מומין, with a temporary or a permanent blemish, receive a share and eat, but they may not offer קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Blemished כהנים, whether the blemish is temporary or permanent, take a share and eat, but they do not offer.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a contrasting case. Unlike the earlier כהנים, a blemished כהן does get a portion and may eat, though he still may not do the עבודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here, not being allowed to serve does not mean losing your share. The משנה adds that it makes no difference whether the blemish will heal or is permanent. The משנה does not explain the reason here.

keyTerms.meaning: כהנים with a physical blemish that keeps them from doing the עבודה.
A temporary blemish that will go away.
A permanent blemish.

steps.whatToRemember: The opening rules of this משנה: a טבול יום, a מחוסר כפורים, and an אונן get no share. An אונן may still touch the meat. בעלי מומין do get a share and eat, but no one in this list may offer.

phrases.english: Blemished priests,
whether temporarily blemished
or permanently blemished,
receive a share and eat,
but do not sacrifice offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין בֵּין בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין עוֹבְרִין בֵּין בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין קְבוּעִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a contrasting case: a כהן who cannot serve yet still receives a share.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בעלי מומין, temporary or permanent, share in and eat the קדשים but may not offer.

steps.title: General rule: no service, no meat; no meat, no hides
steps.stepSummary: The משנה sums up the earlier cases with a rule. A כהן not fit for עבודה gets no share of the meat, and whoever has no share in the meat has no share in the hides.
steps.simpleTranslation: Anyone who is not fit to do the Temple service does not get a share of the meat. And anyone who has no share in the meat has no share in the hides.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives one general rule about who gets a share. It fits the טבול יום, the מחוסר כפורים and the אונן, who cannot serve and get no share. בעלי מומין are the exception from step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The share in the meat depends on being fit to serve. The share in the hides depends on the share in the meat, so it is a chain: service → meat → hides.

keyTerms.meaning: Anyone not fit to do the Temple service
Gets a share, divides along with the others
The meat of the קרבן that the כהנים eat
The hides (skins) of the קרבנות, which also go to the כהנים

steps.confusionAlert: Remember step 12: a בעל מום cannot serve but does eat. So this rule speaks about a כהן who is not fit for a reason like טומאה or being an אונן. It is not about every כהן who is unable to serve.

phrases.english: Anyone who is not fit for the Temple service
does not get a share of the meat.
And anyone who has no share in the meat
has no share in the hides.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a general rule that sums up the cases listed in steps 10-12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eligibility for meat depends on fitness for עבודה, and eligibility for hides depends on eligibility for meat.

steps.title: Impure at the blood, pure at the fats: still no meat
steps.stepSummary: Even a כהן who was טמא only when the blood was sprinkled, and became טהור by the time the fats were burned, gets no share of the meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if he was impure at the time the blood was sprinkled, and pure at the time the fats were burned, he does not get a share of the meat.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה pushes the rule further with a borderline case. It shows that being טהור later in the process is not enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think being טהור for part of the עבודה, the burning of the fats, would earn a share. The משנה says no. What counts is the moment of זריקת הדם, and the next step gives the source for this.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritually impure
Ritually pure
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח, the key act of the קרבן
Burning the fats on the מזבח, a later step

phrases.english: Even if he was impure at the time the blood was sprinkled,
and pure at the time the fats were burned,
he does not get a share of the meat;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the general rule of step 13 to a borderline case of partial טומאה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fitness is measured at the time of זריקת הדם. Being טהור later at the burning of the fats does not earn a share.

steps.title: The source: the meat goes to the one who offers the blood
steps.stepSummary: The משנה proves its ruling from a פסוק. The right thigh of the שלמים belongs to the כהן who offers the blood, so a כהן who could not offer the blood gets no share.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: "The one among the sons of אהרן who offers the blood of the שלמים and the fat, to him shall the right thigh be a portion."
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a פסוק as the source for the ruling in step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links the portion of meat to 'the one who offers the blood.' A כהן who was טמא at the sprinkling could not offer the blood, so he is not included, even if he was fit for the fats later.

keyTerms.meaning: As it says (introducing a פסוק)
Peace offerings, whose meat is shared and eaten
The right thigh, the portion given to the כהנים
A portion, a share

steps.whatToRemember: A כהן's share in the meat and hides depends on his being fit for the עבודה, and the key moment is the sprinkling of the blood. The פסוק gives the portion to 'the one who offers the blood.'
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the right to eat קדשים is tied to the central act of the קרבן, the blood, and not to helping with later steps.

phrases.english: as it says:
"The one who offers the blood of the peace offerings
and the fat, from the sons of Aaron,
to him shall the right thigh be for a portion."
phrases.notes: Some versions have יִהְיֶה, in round brackets. The words in square brackets are the corrected wording, quoting the פסוק exactly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural source for the ruling in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That a כהן טמא at the time of זריקה gets no share of the meat even if he is טהור at the burning of the fats.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 7:33: the portion belongs to 'the one who offers the blood of the שלמים.'
